Dear Colleagues,

## Call for Data: Cancer Incidence in Five Continents - Volume XIII

It is with great pleasure that, on behalf of the International Association of Cancer Registries (IACR) and the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), we invite your cancer registry to submit a dataset for possible inclusion in the forthcoming Volume XIII of Cancer Incidence in Five Continents (CI5-XIII) .

CI5  is  a  longstanding  collaboration  between  IARC  and  IACR  and  remains  a  unique  source  of  cancer incidence  data  from  high-quality  population-based  cancer  registries  around  the  world.  The  principal objective of the series remains as an exposition of comparable cancer incidence based on high-quality data made available by population-based cancer registries worldwide. The recorded incidence data is also a primary source of the GLOBOCAN national estimates in 186 countries, currently available for the year 2024 on the Global Cancer Observatory (GCO).

The new Volume XIII (CI5-XIII) will include incident cancers for the period 2018-2022 and, as previously, published as an online book and abridged pdf. The sets of registry-specific and summary tables available will be similar to those published in Volume XII, based on ICD-10 cancer sites, and, for specific cancer sites, on the 4th digit categories of ICD-10 and on histological subtypes (see Chapters 3 and 4 of Volume XII).

We very  much  encourage  all  population-based  cancer  registries  to  submit  their  data  for  the  specified registration  period,  where  applicable. The  attached  'Call  for  Data'  protocol  provides  all  the  necessary specifications for providing a dataset in response to this call together with relevant explanatory notes. It can also  be  downloaded  in  English,  French  or  Spanish.  Any  enquiries  can be  sent, by e-mail, to ci5@iarc.who.int. Please also see the 'important notes' at the bottom of this letter .

As per the data protocol, those registries included in the previous CI5 Volume (CI5-XII) are encouraged to send incidence data for more recent years where the incidence is considered reasonably complete. The data from these additional years will not be included in the formal CI5 data evaluation process - which exclusively reviews the dataset spanning 2018-22. Instead, the more recent data will be used to showcase the timely and high-quality incidence data available from cancer registries on the GCO on Cancer Over Time.

In summary, the submitted data will populate the following visualisation tools on the IARC/IACR websites:

## [CI5 2.0.](https://www.the-iacr.net/en/ci5-2.0)

- Based on the recorded incidence data as published in the thirteen volumes of CI5 (allowing any erratum corrections  post-publication),  the  focus  is  on  exploring  variations  in  registry-specific  incidence  rates within and across volumes using the data as submitted by registries included in CI5.
- CI5 + . As above, but for registries included in CI5 with data spanning a minimum of 15 consecutive years that  can  provide  more  detailed  data  (e.g.  annual  data,  by  major  histological  groups)  enabling comparisons across selected years and for 180+ diagnostic units. These comprise cancer sites by 3digit  level  ICD-10,  and  for  certain  sites,  by  histological  subtype.  Registers  will  be  able  to  opt  out  of providing such data if they so wish.

## [GCO: Cancer Over Time](https://gco.iarc.who.int/overtime/en)

- The site presents national (or nationally representative) cancer trends based on high-quality routine data. Incidence data will be used for countries with cancer registries included in CI5 and spanning a minimum of 15 consecutive years, based on either national registry data, or one or more subnational registries within the country. As stated above, registries will be able to submit more recent incidence data to ensure the website contains timely incidence data from cancer registries as well as equivalent mortality data from vital registration systems.

1 Sept 2026

## GCO: Cancer Today (GLOBOCAN estimates)

- The data submitted to CI5-XIII may be used indirectly to build future iterations of the biennial GLOBOCAN national estimates.

All datasets submitted to CI5-XIII will be carefully evaluated by the assigned in-house Editorial Board:

- Freddie Bray
- Aude Bardot
- Murielle Colombet
- Les Mery

In addition, we will also invite regional experts to serve as Editors, bringing a needed local focus to the evaluation from the IACR and the Global Initiative for Cancer Registry Development (GICR). Collectively, the Editors will have the task to ensure the published results adhere to the strict quality criteria imposed across volumes.

As with previous CI5 volumes, eligibility to submit data, requires registries to be population-based, voting or associate members of IACR, and to collect information on patients diagnosed with all cancer sites and types in all age groups. Please contact the IACR secretariat or visit the IACR website (https://www.the-iacr.net/) for more information on joining the Association.

All  required  material  described  in  the  call  for  data  can  be  submitted  from  this  point  forward  until 30 November 2026, but early responses will be greatly appreciated. For a submission to be complete, it will be necessary to provide both the dataset and the questionnaire.

The CI5-XIII Editorial Board, the IACR and IARC look forward to working with  population-based cancer registries around the world on this flagship project.

With best wishes,

Dr Freddie Bray Head, Cancer Surveillance Branch brayf@iarc.who.int

## Important notes:

1. A reminder that the closing date for this call is 30 November 2026 .
2. We will use a new Registries Portal developed in REDCap. To access the portal, you will receive  an automated  email  containing  your  username  and  a  link  to  set  your  password.  Please  make  sure  to provide/update the information and contact details for your registry when you first use the Registries Portal (https://csu.datacollect.iarc.who.int/redcap/ ) in the section 'Registry contact s '.
3. Many  population-based  cancer  registries  experienced  operational  disruptions  during  the  COVID-19 pandemic,  particularly  affecting  case  ascertainment  in  2020  and  2021.  During  the  CI5-XIII  review process, evidence of a specific shortfall in cases during one or both years in submitted datasets will be denoted with an asterisk.
4. We have included several items used to estimate survival (vital status and date of last contact) and stage at diagnosis (TNM stage and edition), with related questions incorporated in the questionnaire. Inclusion of these variables should be considered optional in terms of the incidence data submission; the collected data may be used in specific studies coordinated by IARC but only with the prior permission of each cancer registry submitting this data.
5. We recognise that registries  may  face  challenges  sending  the  requested  individual-level  data  given present national data protection regulations. If this is an issue for your registry, please contact us as early as is possible at the above email address.
6. Please send any queries or requests for further information to ci5@iarc.who.int.
